question: the width ladder was retired as 'not quotable'. Turn that direction into a size: how many more names would the median have to clear for this ruler to register a width move, and is that width still a book?

units.step_pp: pp of median CAGR per one-name step inside one cadence
units.slope_pp_per_name: pp of median CAGR per additional name
units.ruler_pp: the baseline grid's median per-cell band (p95-p05)

rule.frozen: written before the first read of the width floor: the axis is the published baseline grid's own medians, the ruler is the same baseline median cell band the buffer floor used, and the sign test runs before the slope

verdict_reasons: 5 of 9 rungs point up (sign agreement 0.556; floor 0.75) -- a line through a hill has a slope, so the sign test runs first
peak width 8 with turnover inside the tested grid = True
slope +0.1138pp per name, r2 0.525 on 4 widths
ruler = median cell band 6.68pp; names of runway required = 58.72
width required = 61.7 (thinnest tested 3 + runway; widest PRICED rung = 20)
the whole ladder spans 0.930pp = 0.139 of the ruler
the rungs disagree about the sign, so no single number of names buys the ruler: width is a trade (CAGR against capacity), not a resolution knob
cross-check on the capacity face's own engine (7 rungs, 0.429 up): sign flips between cadences = True -- a hill that a second engine cannot reproduce is a panel artefact, not a property of width
